content: Crutches are medical devices designed to assist individuals who have sustained injuries to one or both legs or are otherwise unable to bear weight on their lower extremities. These tools provide support and enable mobility when the legs are compromised. The term crutch can also be used metaphorically to describe something that serves as a psychological or emotional support mechanism. It may also refer to an excuse or dependency that prevents an individual from fully engaging in normal life activities. Medical Crutches Types There are various types of medical crutches available, each suited to different needs and conditions. Information on Use Crutches can be used with different gait patterns, depending on the specific reason for their use. For instance, an individual with a leg injury typically employs a swing-to gait. In this method, the injured leg is lifted off the ground, both crutches are placed forward, and the uninjured leg is swung forward to meet the crutches. Other gait patterns are utilized in cases where both legs are equally affected by a disability or when the injured leg is partially weight-bearing. The choice of gait depends on the user’s condition and the level of support required. The term crutch can also function as a verb, describing the act of using crutches for movement. For example, one might say, I am going to crutch to the store, or I will be crutching over to your place. Metaphorically, the word crutch can refer to an object, behavior, or dependency that represents a weakness or a necessity for functioning. For example, one might ask, Can sexuality be used as a social crutch?
